summary_paragraph: A woman with metastatic breast cancer and a history of gastroparesis was admitted with severe nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain, consistent with a gastroparesis flare. She had been recently discharged after a similar admission and was found to have hypokalemia, acidosis, and a urinary tract infection resistant to her outpatient antibiotic, which was treated with IV ceftriaxone. During the hospitalization, she developed C. difficile colitis, requiring oral vancomycin. Her long-acting morphine was adjusted due to concerns about worsening gastroparesis, and she opted to delay GJ tube placement until an outpatient procedure. She improved with IV fluids, antiemetics, and symptom management, and was discharged home on oral medications with follow-up planned for oncology and gastroenterology.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of breast
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
Enterocolitis due to Clostridium difficile, not specified as recurrent
